messages:
incident-bot: :warning: Urgent: decode-pool-phi exhibiting elevated decode latency. p95=380ms (SLO 300ms), p99=980ms, streaming stall count increased by 6x in last 10m. Auto-page -> #eng-oncall.

sanjay: got it. I noticed a canary push earlier today: kernel-release v2.1 with TRT cleanup + flashAttn scheduler tweaks. timeline aligns.

lee: perf dump attached to the dashboard. shapes with seq_len >= 1500 show kernel runtime variance and occasional 400-600ms outliers on CUDA kernels that touch KV cache. https://dash.redwood.internal/d/abc/decode-latency

jamie: stack traces show long waits in the compiled attention path when the dispatcher falls back to the new math path. suspect thread scheduling + TRT fusion path.

rachel: customers reporting streaming stalls and spiky reconnects. support-bot flagged 4 production tenants, two of which are streaming-heavy (acct-omic, acct-sigma).

infra-bot: recent change: rollout kernel-selector@v2.1 -> canary group decode-pool-phi at 12:48 UTC. rollback window until 15:48 UTC.

jamie: quick repro locally: model m-gpt-like, seq=2048, run with flashAttn=on -> intermittent 200-500ms token pause every ~75 tokens. disabled on v2.0 and stalls disappear.

sanjay: mitigation options: A) immediate rollback of kernel-selector to v2.0 on canary (fast), B) enable runtime env SKIP_TRTAttn=1 on pool (hot-fallback), C) route long contexts to backup smaller model temporarily. Thoughts?

lee: B is least invasive. A is straightforward too. C impacts customer quality. Also consider increasing concurrent prefetch to reduce KV misses but that risks memory pressure.

rachel: customers want quick ETA. If we can restore streaming stability in 20-30m that's great; otherwise they want rollback.

infra-bot: executing opt B: applying SKIP_TRTAttn=1 to decode-pool-phi now. Progress 0/18.

infra-bot: progress 9/18 -> nodes switching runtime flags.

infra-bot: complete 18/18 -> SKIP_TRTAttn=1 applied to decode-pool-phi at 1768894600.

jamie: retest synthetic stream at 10m window: p95 dropped to 280ms, p99=340ms. streaming stalls rate back to baseline.

support-bot: acct-omic confirmed reconnects stopped and streaming resumed normally. raising to customer comms.

sanjay: ok monitor for 30m. If stable, propose expanding flag globally for all pools in us-east-1 and opening rollback PR for v2.1. Need to bisect later.

lee: creating runbook snippet for ops to apply flag quickly: ```bash
# quick flip for pool flags
curl -X POST "https://control.internal/pools/decode-pool-phi/flags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"SKIP_TRTAttn":"1"}'
```

jamie: engineering action items: 1) bisect which compile flag + TRT fusion caused scheduling inversion, 2) add long-seq p99 streaming tests to canary gating, 3) add perf counters for KV miss latency per-seq-shape.

infra-bot: monitoring: p95 trending 260-300ms, p99 320-390ms, streaming stall alerts suppressed.

rachel: customer communications: sent note to acct-omic & acct-sigma: "We've applied a temporary runtime mitigation; performance returned to expected levels. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."

sanjay: handoff: taking incident through mitigation and documentation. kristen will take overnight watch starting 20:00 UTC. Kristen please watch p99, streaming disconnects, and any rollback artifacts.

kristen: ack, I'll monitor. escalate to eng-runtime if p99 > 500ms or streaming stall rate jumps >2x.

jamie: for postmortem we should capture the exact tensor shapes that trigger the pathological path and the compile-time heuristics. assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml.

infra-bot: flag remains set. scheduled follow-up: consider global flag rollout at 1768896600 if stable for 60m.

support-bot: closing customer high-severity pings after confirmations at 1768896900.

sanjay: thanks all. I'll open INC-4890 and start doc. leaving the thread for kristen to own overnight. :thumbsup:

kristen: taking ownership. ping me if anything spikes.

incident-bot: MITIGATION APPLIED: runtime fallback enabled for decode-pool-phi. Incident ID INC-4890. Status: monitoring.
